calls.reason: Evidence is thin and mixed: a headline study shows positive, company-focused coverage, while a TIME article explains adoption and quotes critics at length. Nothing shows the alleged pattern broadly.
CNBC confirmed OpenAI expected about $5 billion in 2024 losses on $3.7 billion in revenue. That is company-wide and a projection, but it is well into the billions the speaker described.

The CJR/Tow Center analysis shows ChatGPT passed a million users within days, while significant news coverage came about two months later. Early-adopter tweets also show user-driven enthusiasm, which undercuts 'only because'.
An agenda-setting experiment shows news affects issue priorities. No evidence measures whether shared media narratives largely drive demand for AI coverage.
The only evidence is a Riverside staff interview promoting its AI features. No customer emails or interface records document repeated paid AI upsells.
